questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Culture

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: modulo some initial difficulties, I had an great stay.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The local international office was extremely helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I needed assistance with structuring my semester ie.  choosing courses/professors

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was rather difficult!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Avoid searching for accommodation in Facebook groups. I was shocked by the amount of scam messages I received!
Rather, see if it's possible to join the WhatsApp groups for the Erasmus students. Or as I did, pay one of housing organisations to help (this is rather expensive though!)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Finding housing was far more difficult than I initially thought. In retrospect I should've applied for housing 6 months before the start of my exchange.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not easy. My initial learning agreement was useless as most of the courses were no longer offered or no longer provided in English. Read my comments below for how to avoid headaches in this regard.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
My host university has no comprehensive list of courses offered, rather the different professors have their own websites on which they post their courses and course descriptions. 
I highly recommend contacting the the local institute representatives and ask the for names/links to professors and their courses offered. 
I only found this out upon arrival. Luckily the local representative of the institute of mathematics and the institute of computer science, was very helpful!
With help, I was able to find courses and construct a semester suitable for my degree and interests.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international office can direct you to the relevant professors, who in turn can help with course selection.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Quite successful, however it was initially extremely stressfull and I had to take one class which I didn't find particularly relevant or interesting and which, due to constant changes of the timetable, ended up overlapping with other courses quite a lot.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Université dé Bordeaux has some great professors and courses in mathematics and computer science. My advice is to contact the local international office well in advance. 
They will guide you to the relevant professors who in turn will guide you to the relevant courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I wasn't prepared for the frequent exams, changing timetable and rather messy course registration. Thus the start was quite stressfull, which unfortunately is evident in some of my results.
With that said, the courses were mostly interesting and I've learned a lot!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses are weighted 6- or 3 ECTS and have frequent written exams. If I have to compare the academic level of the courses, I'd say they're about on par with those of my home university.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Many of the courses are divided between two or three professors and two or three subjects relevant to the course.
In most of the courses we didn't have regular exercise classes. Only one or two lectures where the professor would present solutions to a few exercises.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Applied Algorithmics
Advanced Graph Theory 
Game Synthesis and Control
Stochastic Calculus
Supply Chain and Networked Enterprise
French as a foreign language.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Game synthesis and control (Computer science) was extremely interesting and I would highly recommend taking this course if the student is interested in reinforcement learning and/or automata theory. This course has emphasis on the theoretical elements.
In particular the professor Guillaume Lagarde made the course a joy to take. I received a personal reference from one of this professor as well.

Applied Algorithmics (computer science) was also very interesting. 75% of the exam result was based on a rather large and intensive report in which we constructed a graph the the major French highways and applied graph algorithms. Interesting, highly relevant material and great professor. This course is focused on applications.

The French course was a nice change of pace, a great way to learn the language and to meet other international students from different fields of study. Also a great teacher in my particular level.

questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Some groceries are more expensive that I expected, but others are less so. 
All in all I'd say that living expenses are about 85% of those in Denmark

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Far more to do than my schedule allowed for. There's a great student network and countless activities, from running clubs, food clubs ect. to traveling groups and much more. 
If you're bored or feeling alone when on exchange in Bordeaux, it's entirely your own fault.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Travelling- and cultural activities. I met great people from all over the world.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: In particular the mountains, Biarritz and San-Sebastian. Such lovely places!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: quite easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Yes, a couple og trips.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None, although French people speak English quite poorly.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The mannerisms of the local people and the local wine.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Contact the local professors about what courses are offered! and find housing well in advance of your stay!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing comes to mind, but future exchange students are welcome to contact me with any questions.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Some of my academic learnings. The people I met and how much the whole experience has broadened my perspective! I'd love to go back to France and I'll continue to learn the language even though may exchange has now ended.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding my housing and sorting out my courses.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: It was an amazing experience and I highly recommend going to University dé Bordeaux.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
